subject: FinLane — rapid notification, forensic handover & EU transfer clarifications
messages:
From: Marta Kozlowski <marta.kozlowski@finlanebank.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Security Operations <security@finlanebank.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Initial: incident notification timelines & subprocessor evidence request

Hi Olga / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our pre-integration checks we need to confirm Redwood's operational commitments in the DPA around incident notification, evidence access, and any subprocessors that might be involved in forensic investigations. Specifically: 

- What is your proposed "initial notification" window for confirmed breaches affecting personal data? (FinLane expects 48 hours for regulated incidents but will accept a longer window if compensated by strong evidence access).
- How do you define "scope" for a notification (e.g., suspected vs confirmed, PII only vs system-wide incidents)?
- Can Redwood provide short-term read-only access to forensic logs (keystreams, request IDs, full request payloads) for regulator-led investigations or do these go through a formal evidence handover process?
- Which subprocessors (by function) would potentially touch the data needed for an investigation, and can you provide commitments around cross-border transfer assistance?

Attached is our security questionnaire and a draft of the clause we usually propose. Please confirm availability for a quick call the week of 9/13 to resolve remaining points.

Regards,
Marta Kozlowski
Head of Information Security, FinLane Bank

Attachment: FinLane_Security_Questionnaire_20270909.xlsx
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marta Kozlowski <marta.kozlowski@finlanebank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 13:47:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial: incident notification timelines & subprocessor evidence request

Marta,

Thanks for the clear asks and for sending the questionnaire. We're aligned on wanting a tight initial notification window while balancing operational verification to avoid false positives. Quick summary of Redwood's current stance (we can put this into a DPA amendment/redline):

- Initial notification: we propose "48 hours from confirmation of unauthorised access to Personal Data". We do not send preliminary "suspected" alerts unless the incident is escalated and the risk threshold is met; however, we will notify Customers earlier where there is a regulatory requirement.
- Scope: notifications are scoped to confirmed incidents that materially affect Personal Data (PII) or service availability that results in potential leakage; infrastructure incidents without data exposure are treated separately.
- Evidence access: our standard is an evidence handover workflow — secure transfer of logs and forensic artifacts to an agreed escrow or SFTP endpoint after a non-disclosure & lawful handling agreement. We can offer read-only access for regulator-led investigations on a case-by-case basis with proper legal authorisation (subpoena/official request).
- Subprocessors: we maintain a current list in the Console and will include a forensic-access roster for any subprocessors who host logs. We can commit to providing names and data flows within 24 hours of request.

I've attached a redline of an incident clause that mirrors the above. Laura — could Legal confirm whether we can commit to the 48-hour language or need to keep it at 72 business hours for contractability?

Proposed next steps: 1) Confirm clause redline; 2) Agree on evidence transfer mechanism (SFTP vs secure drive vs escrow); 3) DocuSign amendment for DPA.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Head of Privacy Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Proposed_Incident_Clause_redline.docx
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marta Kozlowski <marta.kozlowski@finlanebank.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial: incident notification timelines & subprocessor evidence request

Marta / Olga,

Technical notes to supplement Olga's summary: 

- Logs & timeframe: we retain request/trace logs (full headers + request id + model input hashes) for 90 days by default, with options for extended retention under Dedicated/Private deployments. Forensic artifacts (model state/cached KVs) are ephemeral — preserved only when a forensic snapshot is taken.
- Subprocessor access: typical subprocessors that could be involved in an investigation are (1) cloud storage provider for audit logs, (2) telemetry provider for tracing, and (3) SRE-forensics contract team (external partner). We can provide per-subprocessor scopes and contact liaisons within 24 hours of a request.
- Cross-border movement: if a transfer of raw logs is necessary and contains EU personal data, we will either (a) perform the extraction and transfer under our SCC-compliant process or (b) coordinate with your team to provide an export to a FinLane-controlled location.

Attachment: FinLane_Security_Questionnaire_20270909.xlsx

Happy to discuss specifics on the call.

—Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marta Kozlowski <marta.kozlowski@finlanebank.com>

Cc: Dr. Simon Price <simon.price@regulator.gov.uk>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 07:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial: incident notification timelines & subprocessor evidence request

Thanks Olga / Ben. A few clarifications from FinLane side after internal review and a quick touch with Regulator's office (cc'd Simon):

- Regulator expectation is explicit: for incidents that materially affect personal data, initial notification within 48 hours of "becoming aware" is required. "Becoming aware" can mean internal confirmation or reasonable evidence of exfiltration — it is not limited to fully confirmed root cause.
- We require at least read-access for certain logs to our appointed forensic investigator within the first 7 days. If Redwood cannot provide that read-access, we will require Redwood to provide a full export to a FinLane-controlled secure location within 72 hours.
- Please provide the current list of subprocessors who process logs and their country of processing; the regulator will want to ensure any cross-border transfers are handled under SCCs or equivalent.

We'd like to resolve this before the pilot goes into staging. Are you available for a 30-minute slot today 14:30 UTC?

Best,
Marta
Head of Information Security, FinLane Bank
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 16:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial: incident notification timelines & subprocessor evidence request

Marta — thanks and appreciated for looping Simon. Short summary and commitments we can get into an amendment: 

1) Initial notification: Redwood will provide an initial notification within 48 hours of becoming aware of an incident materially affecting Personal Data. The notification will include: summary of affected data classes, initial estimate of user count (if known), affected services/regions, and immediate mitigation steps.

2) Evidence access & handover: Redwood will either provide (a) read-only access to requested logs to your appointed forensic investigator for a 7-day window OR (b) a full secure export to a FinLane-controlled SFTP within 72 hours (your preference). We will execute a standard forensic transfer agreement before any direct access.

3) Subprocessors & transfers: list of subprocessors and processing countries will be provided within 24 hours of final amendment signature. Any cross-border exports will follow SCCs; we can also perform the extraction inside EU regions and ship to your controlled endpoint if required.

4) Detailed report: a full technical incident report (root cause, forensics, remediation plan) will follow within 30 days of initial notification, with periodic updates as needed.

Next actions: Laura to prepare the DPA amendment with 48-hour language + evidence access options (read-access vs export) and attach the forensic transfer agreement template. Marta — please confirm whether you prefer read-access (option a) or export (option b) for the pilot. I've also started a DocuSign envelope to capture the amendment once we align.
